topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional local interventions and systemic cytotoxic chemotherapies alongside the physiological challenges and resistance mechanisms associated with them.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell vulnerabilities and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that capitalize on intrinsic cancer cell defects, including hormone dependence, checkpoint loss, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the rationale of oncogene addiction, the design of small-molecule kinase inhibitors, and the evolutionary pathways through which tumors develop drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on using engineered antibodies to selectively target cancer cell surface antigens and deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell based interventions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biological basis of antitumor immune surveillance and the therapeutic approaches designed to reactivate or genetically engineer T cells.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader trajectory of cancer care, reflecting on historical survival trends, systemic clinical challenges, and future management paradigms.
